question.problem: Find the arc length of the polar curve $r={3}^{\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \pi .$
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={3}^{\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }={3}^{\theta }\operatorname{ln}⁡3.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{({3}^{\theta })}^{2}+{({3}^{\theta }\operatorname{ln}⁡3)}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{{3}^{2\theta }+{3}^{2\theta }{ln}^{2}⁡3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(1+{ln}^{2}⁡3){3}^{2\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{3}^{\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡3}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot {3}^{\theta }{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡3}\cdot \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\cdot ({3}^{\pi }-{3}^{0}) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{1+{ln}^{2}⁡3}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}({3}^{\pi }-1).\end{aligned}
$$
